strengths: Comprehensive quantitative analysis of visual complexity's impact on attention entropy, with clear correlation demonstrated across texture and color dimensions (Section 3, Figs. 4-5)
Extensive experimental validation: 7 datasets, 4+ VLM families, rigorous ablations, statistical testing (bootstrap CI, McNemar's test on V*), and recent model evaluation
Training-free method applicable to existing VLMs without retraining, with consistent improvements across diverse models and architectures
Strong empirical results on perception-heavy tasks: +27.8% on V* (LLaVA-1.5-7B), +9.33% on TextVQA, scaling with visual perception demands
Theoretical framework with closed-form solution and rigorous proofs; multiplicative decomposition empirically validated over additive alternative (Table 10, Appendix G)
Excellent presentation: clear visualizations (Figs. 2, 6, 8), comprehensive appendix with implementation details, and honest limitations discussion
weaknesses: Assumption 1 (multiplicative decomposition A = F_vis ⊗ F_sem) is idealized and simplified from softmax(QK^T/√d); validity in practice not rigorously characterized, and gap between theory and implementation not formally analyzed

Uniformity assumption (F_sem(G,I) ≈ 1_Nv) only approximately holds with KL divergence = 0.147, which is non-negligible; paper acknowledges degradation on high visual complexity but provides no formal analysis
Explicit failure on global spatial reasoning tasks (Fig. 11 depth estimation); method limited to local fine-grained perception, reducing applicability scope
Task-dependent effectiveness: gains range from +24% (DocVQA) to +0.6% (ScienceQA); no principled guidance for hyperparameter selection (p, K) on new domains
Complexity metrics are simplistic (Canny edges for texture, hue histogram for color) and lack theoretical grounding; unclear generalization beyond natural images
Significant inference overhead: 3× GPU time (Table 6); early termination potential (~7% theoretical savings, Appendix C.4) unvalidated in practice; may limit deployment

Several methodological choices lack clear justification: general instruction selection appears somewhat arbitrary despite ablation; why layers [20,25] work universally unexplained; layer-wise entropy trend in Fig. 5b lacks causal interpretation
Core insight (visual complexity disperses attention, masking helps) is somewhat intuitive; theoretical novelty is limited beyond straightforward multiplicative decomposition

Experimental gaps: V* has only 191 samples (small despite statistical testing); TextVQA OCR-free protocol limits comparisons; attention extraction details underdescribed; limited comparison with ViCrop beyond Table 5
Fails on important task categories (multi-image reasoning, global context reasoning); single-image single-question limitation constrains applicability

strengths: Thorough and well-presented empirical analysis connecting visual complexity, attention entropy, and performance degradation (Section 3) with clear visualizations and systematic experiments
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 7 diverse datasets and multiple VLM architectures (Qwen2.5, LLaVA-1.5, Qwen3, Gemma) with rigorous ablations and statistical significance testing
Training-free and broadly applicable approach without requiring model fine-tuning; demonstrates consistent improvements across all evaluated models and datasets
Honest discussion of limitations, including failure cases on global reasoning tasks (Fig. 11) and restricted applicability to localization-focused tasks

Excellent presentation and organization with well-motivated visualizations, clear logical flow, and comprehensive supplementary material including proofs, implementation details, and extended experiments
weaknesses: Weak theoretical foundation: Assumption 1 (multiplicative attention decomposition) lacks rigorous justification; paper explicitly states theory is 'intended to motivate design rather than describe exact properties' (p.22), undermining theoretical contribution; uniformity assumption (KL=0.147) is approximate with unexplored impact; connection between 'visual complexity' and 'visual noise' is conceptually problematic—complex images contain information, not inherent noise

Limited technical novelty: Core idea of masking images for VLM improvement is established (ViCrop [38]); contrastive attention comparison is straightforward; Table 3-5 show marginal gains over ViCrop (58.2% vs. 56.06% on TextVQA), not clearly justifying added complexity

Significant computational overhead requires 3× GPU time per sample (1.3s vs. 0.4s baseline, Table 6); appendix optimizations (early termination ~7%, caching up to 37%) are theoretical, not implemented; overhead poorly justified given modest improvements on high-baseline tasks (0.6% ScienceQA, 1.8% ChartQA)

Restricted applicability and inconsistent gains: Method fails on global spatial reasoning (Fig. 11); gains scale with visual perception demands (TextVQA +8.9% vs. ScienceQA +0.6% for Qwen2.5-VL-7B); substantial variation across model families (Table 1) lacks explanation

Hyperparameter complexity and generalization concerns: Five hyperparameters (L, T, p, K, λ) with Figure 7 showing 2-3% sensitivity to p and K; fixed L=[20,25] assumed universal despite models having different depths; general instruction selection (Table 9) appears somewhat arbitrary with only marginal improvements over alternatives

Insufficient empirical validation of core claims: Decomposition not validated (Table 11 only shows uniformity, not multiplicative structure); additive vs. multiplicative ablation (Table 4) validates design choice but not theory; missing ablation on direct A^(Q) masking beyond brief Table 4 entry

Experimental design issues: V* benchmark (191 samples) emphasized despite small size; only V* results include confidence intervals—main datasets (Table 1) lack significance testing; baseline comparisons (Table 5) limited to single model; no significance tests on A-OKVQA, POPE, TextVQA

Logical gaps in core mechanism: Paper demonstrates attention entropy correlates with performance (Fig. 5a) but doesn't establish causation; why masking improves performance isn't deeply justified theoretically—removes context alongside noise; time step choice (t_end > T_full) lacks thorough explanation

Reproducibility concerns: Results depend critically on specific prompt 'Write a general description'; layer range L=[20,25] may not generalize across different model architectures; attention extraction details (which heads, averaging method) underspecified; model-specific tuning contradicts 'training-free' framing

Oversimplified theoretical framing: Paper claims 'visual noise' causes dispersion, but high texture/color complexity reflects information density, not noise; for TextVQA (cluttered stores), complex visual information is task-relevant; this conceptual issue undermines theoretical motivation

strengths: Clear and well-motivated empirical analysis showing visual complexity correlates with attention entropy and performance degradation, with rigorous quantitative validation across 7 datasets and 4 VLM architectures

Comprehensive experimental validation including extensive ablation studies, statistical significance testing (bootstrap CIs, McNemar's test), and honest limitation discussion with concrete failure cases
Training-free, practical method that consistently improves VLM performance on perception-heavy tasks (TextVQA +9.33%, V* +27.8%) without requiring fine-tuning or external tools

Thorough and well-documented work with clear presentation, detailed appendices, algorithm specification, and transparent discussion of tradeoffs (inference overhead, scope limitations, hyperparameter sensitivity)
Solid theoretical framework (attention decomposition) with formal derivations and empirical validation of key assumptions, though simplifying in nature
Systematic analysis of how performance scales with task type, with gains proportional to visual perception demands, indicating task-dependent effectiveness is well-understood
weaknesses: Core theoretical assumptions (multiplicative decomposition A^(Q)=Fvis⊗Fsem and uniform general attention) are simplifications that don't capture softmax's nonlinear interactions; while empirically justified, theoretical foundation is softer than presented

Significant practical overhead: 3x slower inference (1.0-1.3s vs 0.17s per sample) and +0.6-3.2GB memory increase; proposed optimizations (early termination, caching) are theoretical only, not implemented

Limited applicability scope: method fails on tasks requiring global spatial context (depth ordering, spatial relationships) and provides minimal gains on knowledge-based reasoning (ScienceQA +0.60-5.93%), constraining general-purpose utility
Despite 'training-free' label, method involves multiple hyperparameters (L, T, p, λ, K) and general instruction prompt selection matters (±3% variance in Appendix D), requiring task-dependent tuning

Incremental technical novelty: combines existing techniques (attention contrasting, masking/cropping from ViCrop) without fundamental new insights; main contribution is application to visual complexity problem

Incomplete analysis of key assumptions: no theoretical justification for why general instructions yield uniform attention, no systematic study of when uniformity assumption breaks down or sensitivity to image resolution

V* benchmark concerns: only 191 examples; dramatic gains may partly reflect dataset design that perfectly matches method's strengths (fine-grained search in clutter); limited baseline comparisons (external tools evaluated on one dataset only)
